Select an animal sprite and program it to move from its starting position to the target item without touching the marked water tiles.
Count the grid squares: if the frog needs to move 6 squares, change the number in the block from 1 to 6, and put the number in one block instead of snapping a long train of Move Right 1 blocks.
reference.materials: Tech Log notebook, ScratchJr with its grid icon, animal sprite

reference.name: Catching game or maze prototype
steps: Warm-up: discuss giving polite feedback with the Plus/Delta system (one thing that works well, one suggestion).
Tech log: document the structure of the final design, tracking the control loops and event input triggers used.
Practical task: build an interactive catching game or maze navigation prototype using count-controlled loops for set-up, infinite loops for movement and clear input/output responses.
Peer review loop: rotate chairs to test classmates' projects.
Final tech log: write one feature enjoyed in a classmate's project and one new coding concept to explore next term.
